ops.text: A manual `plugin.json` version bump rode along in an unrelated commit (f0f5423, "chore: repin daemonkit") without a release tag, defeating the whole point of `AUTOBUMP_GUARD` for binary-pinned plugins: automation refuses exactly this bump, but nothing stops a human/agent commit from doing it, and the only detection is the weekly strict autobump run — up to 6 days of every user paying a synchronous `brew upgrade` on each MCP/hook startup, with intermittent full MCP-toolset loss when it crosses the 30s connect timeout. A guard (capt-hook or CI) that rejects plugin.json version changes in commits that don't also tag, or a strict autobump on every push for guarded plugins, would have caught this the same morning.
